focus_areas.finding: accounts_service/jwt_secret.py was implemented in Phase 186C. load_jwt_secret() checks ATLAS_AUTH_JWT_SECRET and ATLAS_JWT_SECRET env vars first, then reads/creates a persisted file at {ATLAS_ACCOUNTS_DATA_DIR}/auth/jwt_secret with mode 0o600. The critical instability (random secret on every restart) documented in Phase 186B is closed.
No session or email-token pruning existed. Sessions and EmailTokens accumulated indefinitely.
focus_areas.implementation: Created accounts_service/session_cleanup.py with prune_sessions(), prune_email_tokens(), and prune_all(). Wired into _startup() in main.py. Added POST /admin/maintenance/prune (superadmin only) for manual operator triggers. Revoked sessions are retained for 7 days (audit trail) before deletion.

focus_areas.finding: INITIAL_ADMINS was parsed in config.py but _startup() in main.py never called any bootstrap logic. There was no way to create the first superadmin without direct DB access.
focus_areas.implementation: Created accounts_service/bootstrap.py with bootstrap_superadmins(db) that promotes ATLAS_INITIAL_ADMINS emails to superadmin role at startup. Idempotent, audit-logged, no API surface. Wired into _startup() in main.py.

sections: Investigating a login or device issue

residual_risks: Session cleanup runs at startup only (no background scheduler). For production beyond beta, a cron job or APScheduler should call POST /admin/maintenance/prune periodically.
bootstrap_superadmins only promotes users who are already registered. If the operator's email is not yet in the DB, they must register first, then restart the service.
ATLAS_INITIAL_ADMINS should be removed from the environment after the first successful bootstrap to reduce attack surface. The promotion persists in the DB regardless.

The maintenance/prune endpoint commits its own transaction then immediately writes the audit entry in a second commit. In a race condition with concurrent prunes, both audit entries will be written — harmless but verbose.

accounts_state.json (desktop) is written without file locking under ThreadingHTTPServer — race condition under concurrent desktop HTTP requests is a known issue from Phase 186B, not addressed in this phase.
